purpose: Avoid the per-frustum pickPosition depth copy for flat ellipsoid geography while preserving rendered quality and object selection.

sources.finding: useDepthPicking gates PickDepth update and executeCopyDepth after translucent rendering.
A full-size color framebuffer and viewport quad pack the depth texture for position readback.
Controller compares depth and globe-ray intersections, retaining the globe ray when depth is undefined.
pickPositionWorldCoordinates returns undefined with useDepthPicking false; object pick/drillPick are distinct.

method.visual: Sequential on/off/on in the same page with real final imagery, idle camera, loaded tiles, fonts ready and three loaded postRender frames per capture; compare every RGBA byte and dimensions. No quality or geometry setting changes.
method.contexts: Nine existing quality/device profiles per renderer, sequential contexts; finite 256-entry/8-MiB real imagery test cache; no production observer.
method.redraw: Eight 3-second fixed-camera forced-redraw windows, ABBA ABBA, software desktop auto-low, same page and settings. Passive bounded wrapper counts native PickDepth.executeCopyDepth calls; restored after each window. Not active camera navigation or startup timing.
method.allocation: Two fresh current-source app pages, desktop auto-low and mobile auto, read depth flag and pinned private pickDepths count before on/off/on. No prototype alteration or constructor interception.
method.bounds: At most 16 page errors per case, one context at a time, finite capture deadlines; listeners/timers/wrappers and own browser/server cleaned. Sources retained outside production/precache.

redrawSummary.interpretation: Small noisy difference, not evidence of an active FPS improvement. Each observed enabled frame copied depth once; disabled windows copied zero times.

rejectedIdleHypothesis.conclusion: Clock shouldAnimate is false. After settling, baseline and Infinity both render zero frames at rest. Initial six frames were not attributable to the clock; do not claim idle-redraw savings or alter maximumRenderTimeChange based on this experiment.

focusedValidation.native: map-performance new constructor regression failed before change and passed with green-coding suite after change.
focusedValidation.browser: Existing reduced-motion flow passed in 16522 ms on Chrome 155 Windows: desktop/mobile wheel zoom, object selection, instant/animated transitions and live reduced-motion preference. The final public flag assertion is covered in the following full gate.

limitations: Chrome 155 Windows/Intel and Windows/SwiftShader are not Chromium 151 Linux, a physical phone, or a release gate.
No direct GPU allocation bytes, CPU/GPU time, energy, CO2 or active FPS saving was measured. Texture counts and eliminated copy calls are resource indicators.
Flat EllipsoidTerrainProvider and zero-height countries make the native globe-ray fallback appropriate. Future elevated terrain, models or a pickPosition feature must revisit useDepthPicking.

The camera fallback may differ numerically from packed depth at pixel edges; identical static RGBA does not prove identical camera trajectories. Real wheel and drag behavior requires browser validation.
No startup timeout cause is established; original readiness, quality, deadlines and budgets remain required.
